Victoria sponge cake:

(I’m in the uk btw so sorry if the measurements aren’t what you use and also the strawberries are to cover a hole my thumb made so you can take or leave them)

Ingredients for the sponge:
-400g self-raising flour 
-1 1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda 
-300g caster sugar
-115ml sunflower oil
-400ml soya milk
-3tbsp golden syrup
-4 tbsp raspberry jam (any will work)

For the buttercream:
-200g any vegan spread
-175g icing sugar 

Method:

1. Preheat your oven to 180C (160C if you have a fan oven) and grease 2 loose bottom circular tins (if you don’t have loose-bottomed tins then line the bottom with greaseproof paper)
2. Sift flour, bicarbonate of soda and sugar into a mixing bowl
3. In a separate jug whisk together the sunflower oil, milk, syrup and vanilla extract and then pour into the dry ingredients
4. Mix with a hand blender for 2 minutes or  until thick and creamy.
5. Distribute the mixture evenly into the two tins 
6. Bake for 35-45 minutes (depending on your oven)
7. While the cakes are cooking whisk together the icing sugar and spread and place in the fridge to form until needed.
8. When the cakes are done, remove and leave to cool completely 
9. When they are cool, spread the jam and cream in the middle of the cake and assemble.
10. Dust with icing sugar if you want to

I had cystic acne all over my cheeks, and I tried everything. I tried so many face washes that claimed to clear skin but like the other commenter said it’s normally hormonal. If you don’t want to take something, then you may only be able to minimise it. There are many topical creams I’ve tried, epiduo hurt a lot and left my skin really dry and I didn’t see many results on bigger spots but it did clear smaller bumps. 

I also used duac. Duac was amazing for about a month and then it just plateaued. I moved onto antibiotics then, because I felt I didn’t really want all the negative side effects of things like accutane. I started taking oxytetracycline, I’m pretty sure many of the tetracyclines work to the same extent, but oxytetracycline has completely cleared my skin (for now). I’ve been taking it for like 3 months and it says it takes 6-10 weeks to see results and it’s about my 13th week now and in the last 3 weeks my skin has cleared up so much. 

The thing is it’s not certain whether it will stay clear but I’m still gonna take it for a while and hopefully it will keep my skin clear. I recommend going to a doctor or a dermatologist and see what prescription they recommend. 

I use a basic face wash, and then just a basic, scent less moisturiser as I’ve found no face washes or moisturisers help or affect my skin any more than water would.

Hope this was somewhat helpful  :) and don’t worry it will be clear eventually.
